h: Bransholme and beyond: making it part of a Hull day
p: Bransholme is a big housing estate, built in the 1960s and 1970s on the north-eastern edge of Hull, and North Point sits right at its heart on Goodhart Road. It's a proper community hub, so expect locals doing their weekly shop rather than tourists, and that's part of its no-nonsense charm.
Getting here is easy enough. Buses run regularly between Bransholme and Hull city centre, and if you're driving, the centre is close to the main routes in and out of the north of the city.

The real reason to head into Hull, though, is the city itself, which has some cracking free attractions. In the Old Town, the Museums Quarter on the High Street includes the Streetlife Museum, with its old trams, carriages and recreated street, and Wilberforce House, birthplace of the anti-slavery campaigner William Wilberforce. The Hull and East Riding Museum covers everything from mammoths to Romans. The Ferens Art Gallery, on Queen Victoria Square, has an impressive collection and is free too.

For something with a wow factor, The Deep, the aquarium on the Humber, is the city's big-ticket family day out. The Humber Bridge, to the west of the city, is a spectacular sight, and you can walk part of the way across for views of the estuary. Hull Minster, in the heart of the Old Town, is a magnificent church that's worth a look. Use North Point for supplies and a cuppa, then head into town for the headline acts.
